newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso re-election moves closer in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso re-election moves closer in Brazil.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's bid to become Brazil's first re-elected leader received a major boost on Wednesday when the senate approved a bill allowing him to run again.

A constitutional amendment, which would allow sitting presidents, state governors and mayors to seek second consecutive terms, was approved by 63 senators, more than the three-fifths or 49 of the senators needed.
"The margin was way above expectations," said political analyst Ricardo Pedreira.
The bill has been approved by the lower house of Congress, but it must pass through a second vote in the senate later to become law.

Some senators, considering running for governor in the next election, had demanded assurances from the government that incumbent governors and mayors would have to resign six months before seeking re-election.
It was not immediately clear how this would be dealt with, because the government maintained that an existing law required governors and mayors, but not presidents, to resign.
Cardoso has made the re-election bill one of the central planks of his programme.

The senate approval of the re-election bill gave a boost to Cardoso. His popularity has dipped recently due to discontent with the government's adjustment of the minimum wage and its handling of a municipal bonds scandal.
Brazil has banned re-election since the founding of the republic in 1889 to prevent a repeat of the supreme powers of its Portuguese rulers.

But Cardoso says he wants to win the 1998 presidential race to give political continuity to the economic reforms he launched as finance minister in 1994, which have brought inflation down from 5,000 percent a year to just 10 percent in 1996.

The prospect of Cardoso's re-election is seen as bolstering his support in Congress and would make it easier for his government to push through his reforms of the civil service, tax and pensions, considered vital to the long-term success of his economic plan.
